Canada's stock market just had one of its worst days of the year — and it landed right in RRSPs and TFSAs.

The S&P/TSX composite fell about 737 points Wednesday, roughly 2% — its third straight drop (Canadian Press, Nov. 18). Gold and oil both tumbled, and because the index is packed with miners, energy and banks, the dividend stocks most Canadians hold fell together.

One upside: January crude slid to about US$82 a barrel, pointing to cheaper gas ahead.

My take: a resource-heavy index cuts both ways — it sinks your RRSP on a day like this, but cheaper oil quietly helps at the pump.

Does a day like this change how you invest?
